chunks: Ali, from his father, from Salih ibn Sa'id, elevated it, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:

I asked him about a man who steals, so his hand is cut off by the establishment of proof against him, but he did not return what he stole. How should one deal with the property of the man from whom he stole? Is it not upon him to return it? And if he claims that he has nothing left, neither little nor much, and that is known to be from him? He said: He is made to work until he pays back the last dirham he had stolen.

key_terms.آخِرَ دِرْهَمٍ: The last dirham (emphasizing completeness of payment)
key_terms.رَدُّهُ: Returning (the stolen goods or their value)
key_terms.يُسْتَسْعَى: He is made to work/compelled to labor

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a thief's liability for stolen property after hand amputation if he claims to have no money?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between the fixed hadd punishment of amputation and the separate right of the owner (haqq al-mal) to restitution, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence. It establishes that the thief's liability is not extinguished by the physical penalty, requiring him to pay the full value of the stolen goods even if he must work until he pays the last dirham. This ruling underscores the comprehensive nature of financial justice in Islamic law, ensuring the victim is fully compensated regardless of the thief's current asset status.
